pool: Titan has a cycle of methane clouds, rain, rivers, and evaporation resembling Earth's water cycle.
Ring-tailed lemurs hold their tails upright like flags to help a traveling group stay together.
Sloth bears do not hibernate.
Unlike many lizards, prehensile-tailed skinks cannot shed their tails to escape a predator.
German chocolate cake takes its name from chocolate associated with Samuel German, not from Germany.
A giant anteater's tongue is attached to its breastbone.
Naked mole-rats can eat the inside of a large tuber while leaving enough alive for it to keep growing.

Saturn's main rings are extraordinarily flat, with an average thickness of roughly ten meters.
The Moon's early crust formed partly from lighter minerals floating on a global magma ocean.
Small traces of gold have been found in the leaves of Eucalyptus trees.
Only a few poison frog species have documented traditional use in poisoning hunting darts.
Measurements of Enceladus's slight wobble helped reveal that its underground ocean is global.
Red pandas leave scent trails using glands on the bottoms of their feet.
Theophilus Van Kannel patented a revolving door in the United States in 1888.
Ganymede has a thin atmosphere containing oxygen, far too tenuous to breathe.
Sloth bears can delay implantation of a fertilized egg, extending the time between mating and birth.
Much of the ice sprayed by Enceladus falls back onto the moon as snow.
Curiosity played Happy Birthday using its sample-analysis instrument on the first anniversary of its Mars landing.
Tokay geckos grip surfaces with microscopic filaments on their toes rather than suction cups.
Reflectors left on the Moon let researchers measure its distance by timing returning laser pulses.
Hellbenders have no eyelids.
Despite its name, the Panamanian golden frog belongs to the true toad family.
The "Star Spangled Banner" did not become a national anthem until 1931. It was designated by an Act of Congress.
Tonga has issued banana-shaped postage stamps.
Neptune has clumps within its rings called arcs, with names including Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity.
A prehensile-tailed porcupine is born with its eyes open and is already able to climb.
January takes its name from Janus, the Roman god associated with doorways and transitions.
Triton was discovered just 17 days after Neptune.
The melody of The Star-Spangled Banner originally belonged to a British song called To Anacreon in Heaven.
The Sun's equator rotates faster than its poles.
A comet can have two distinct tails: one of dust and one of electrically charged gas.
A naked mole-rat colony's tunnels can extend for several kilometers.
About 50 kilometers above Venus's surface, atmospheric pressure is similar to Earth's sea-level pressure.
Despite being called bearcats, binturongs are neither bears nor cats.
Uranus is wider than Neptune but has less mass.
Large raindrops flatten as they fall; they do not have the teardrop shape used in drawings.
Uranus's magnetic axis is tilted about 60 degrees from its rotation axis.
Prehensile-tailed porcupines can make sounds ranging from coughs and whines to barks and shrieks.
Fishing cats have a dense inner layer of fur that keeps water away from their skin.
Giant pandas continue to defecate while resting, leaving clues to how long they occupied a spot.
Humans can learn to navigate using echoes from sounds such as tongue clicks.
Jupiter is the fastest spinning planet in the solar system (it only takes about 10 hours to complete a full rotation on its axis).
Adult sloth bears lack their two upper front incisors, leaving a gap that helps them suck up insects.
Some tarantulas share burrows with tiny frogs that eat insects threatening the spiders' eggs.
During World War II, the United States tested a weapon that would release bats carrying small incendiary devices.
Sand cats hunt venomous snakes, including vipers.
Juno's measurements suggest Jupiter's core is diffuse rather than a neatly separated solid ball.
Red pandas wrap their long tails around themselves for warmth while resting.
Specialized ankle joints let clouded leopards climb down trees headfirst.
A Japanese white pine trained as a bonsai since 1625 survived Hiroshima and now lives at the U.S. National Arboretum.
Jupiter's neighboring cloud bands often blow in opposite directions.
Red pandas can rotate their ankles to climb down trees headfirst.
NASA's Stardust mission brought particles from Comet Wild 2 back to Earth in 2006.
The Moon's far side gets sunlight too; it is not permanently dark.
Wood frogs retain urea during winter, helping their bodies tolerate freezing.
An April Fools' prank in 1974 used burning tires to make Alaska's Mount Edgecumbe look as if it were erupting.
Friedrich Miescher isolated DNA in 1869, long before its role in heredity was understood.
Clouded leopards have the longest canine teeth relative to skull size of any living wild cat.
Mary Anderson patented a hand-operated windshield cleaner in 1903.
Elephant shrews are not true shrews; another name for them is sengis.
Camels have a third, translucent eyelid that helps protect their eyes from sand.
Amman was known as Philadelphia during the Hellenistic and Roman periods.
Binturongs can chuckle and purr.
Some flying foxes have wingspans approaching two meters.
Green anacondas give birth to live young rather than laying eggs.
Titan is larger than the planet Mercury.
NASA reused the original tapes containing Apollo 11's slow-scan television signal; converted broadcast recordings survived.
Growing an apple from seed usually produces a genetically different variety; named varieties are commonly propagated by grafting.
Sunlight breaks down methane in Titan's atmosphere, so something must replenish it over time.
Venus takes longer to turn once on its axis than to travel once around the Sun.
Mercury's craters are named for artists, musicians, and writers, including Dr. Seuss.
Fennec fox dens can have tunnels ten meters long, with multiple escape exits.
Lake Baikal, in Siberia, is the deepest lake in the world.
Titan's orange haze is produced by chemical reactions involving methane and nitrogen high in its atmosphere.
The solar wind carries the Sun's magnetic field outward in a spiral resembling water from a rotating sprinkler.
Fossils show that penguins lived in New Zealand about 62 million years ago.
Ganymede has auroras around its poles.
Kobuk Valley in Alaska has sand dunes that rise about 100 feet above the surrounding landscape.
Titan's surface is so cold that water ice behaves much like rock.
Mercury's iron core takes up about 85 percent of the planet's radius.
A piece of wood from the tree associated with Newton's apple story traveled aboard space shuttle Atlantis in 2010.
